# A pocket guide to bread

A made-up guide for the compiler's tests: three short lessons in two tabs, and one extra module, so the compiler has a contents page, tabs, cards and links across pages to draw.

> [!module|basics] Baking basics

Two lessons to start with, and a third once those feel easy. The extras are in [[extras.booklet]].

> [!tab|start] Start here

Pick a morning when you are at home all day.

> [!tab|go] Go further

Once the first loaf works, [[#Crust and colour]] is the next step.

> [!activity|flour tab:start icon:clock] Flour and water
> A morning's work

Flour, water, salt and time make a dough. Wait for it to rise, then read [[#Resting]] below.

## Resting

Cover the bowl and leave it alone for an hour.

> [!activity|shaping parent:flour tab:start] 🍞 Shaping the loaf

Fold the dough over itself twice, then turn it seam side down. Go back to [[#Flour and water]] if it feels dry.

> [!tip]- A trick with a spoon
> Wet the spoon first, so the dough lets go.

> [!activity|crust tab:go] Crust and colour

A hot oven and a pan of water give a crisp, brown crust.[^oven]

> [!choice|steam] What does the pan of water do?
- [ ] It makes steam
- [ ] It cools the oven

> [!hint]- Hint
> Think about what hot water does.

Next, see [[#Go further]], or start again at [[#Start here]].

> [!activity|notes hidden] Hidden notes

Never on the page.

[^oven]: *The Little Oven Book*, 2nd edition (2019), p. 12: "Steam keeps the crust soft while the loaf springs." Verified 2026-10-01.
